title: Bulb Switcher II
summary: Given n bulbs labeled from 1 to n initially turned on, and four buttons that flip the status of bulbs based on their labels.
statement: Given n bulbs labeled from 1 to n initially turned on, and four buttons that flip the status of bulbs based on their labels. Each button press must be one of the four types, and the total number of presses is fixed. Determine the number of distinct final bulb statuses achievable after exactly presses button presses.
constraints: Count configurations reachable after exactly presses button presses using the four specified flip patterns.
reference_solution:
def distinct_bulb_states(n, presses):
    if presses == 0: return 1
    n = min(n, 3)
    if n == 1: return 2
    if n == 2: return 3 if presses == 1 else 4
    if presses == 1: return 4
    if presses == 2: return 7
    return 8

hints: Only the first three bulb positions create independent behavior under the four periodic buttons.
Reduce n to three and use the small closed-form state counts by press count.
Handle zero presses, then n=1, n=2, and presses 1/2/3+ for n>=3.
Beyond three bulbs every position repeats one of the same parity/modulo-three patterns, so no new state distinctions arise.

tests.explanation: Either flipping all bulbs or one of the equivalent odd-position controls creates two distinct states.
One press can reach three distinct two-bulb configurations.
